entities.label: Institution
entities.summary:
The International Earth Rotation and Reference Systems Service (IERS), established in 1987, plays a crucial role in defining and maintaining the global standards for time and reference frames that underpin modern navigation and communication systems. With headquarters in Paris, France, this organization emerged from the necessity of precise timekeeping as the world transitioned into an age where satellites and global positioning systems became integral to everyday life. The IERS is instrumental in ensuring that our understanding of time and space remains synchronized, thereby facilitating international cooperation in scientific research and technology development.

The establishment of the IERS was fueled by advancements in astrophysics, geodesy, and the growing reliance on satellite technology. In 1984, the International Union of Geodesy and Geophysics (IUGG) convened a meeting in Paris where the need for a unified approach towards global timekeeping was recognized. Consequently, the IERS was founded to provide the scientific community with accurate data on the Earth’s rotation and to define reference systems, such as International Terrestrial Reference Frame (ITRF), which has undergone several iterations since its inception. These contributions have enabled precise navigation and have been fundamental for industries ranging from telecommunications to aerospace.
